15# Kunlunxin (XPU) override of ``flag_gems.ops._dirichlet_grad``. 

16# 

17# The generic implementation maps a scalar ``_dirichlet_grad_one`` over the 

18# tile with ``tl.map_elementwise`` (Triton >= 3.6) to get lazy ``if -> return`` 

19# control flow. The XPU backend has no lowering for the resulting 

20# ``tt.map_elementwise`` op, so ``PassManager::run`` fails with 

21# ``failed to legalize operation 'tt.map_elementwise'``. 

22# 

23# This override keeps the exact ATen ``dirichlet_grad_one`` math but evaluates 

24# it in plain vectorized Triton (``tl.where`` based selection instead of scalar 

25# control flow), which lowers on XPU. Branch selection happens at the end, so 

26# every branch is evaluated for every element; that is the trade-off for not 

27# depending on ``tt.map_elementwise``. 

28# 

29# Two further XPU constraints shaped the code below: 

30# * The XPU libdevice exposes ``log``/``exp`` (and the fp64 variants of 

31# ``tan``/``pow``/``div_rn``) as ``Unsupported`` stubs that fail at link 

32# time, and ``log1p`` trips ``triton_xpu.unpack reached lowering without a 

33# bufPtr``. Everything is therefore built from core ``tl`` math ops 

34# (``tl.log``/``tl.exp``/``tl.sqrt``/``tl.floor``/``tl.sin``/``tl.cos``, 

35# with ``exp(b*log(a))`` standing in for ``pow``). 

36# * The device has no fp64 (torch silently stores everything as fp32), so the 

37# saddle-point branch is evaluated in fp32 against a double-precision 

38# reference. ``_log1p`` plus the ``fma``-based ``axbx`` below keep the 

39# cancellation in ``beta*log(beta/(total*(1-x))) + alpha*log(alpha/(total*x))`` 

40# from blowing past the test tolerance. 

41

53@triton.jit 

54def _div_rn(a, b): 

55 # IEEE round-to-nearest division (matches the reference ``accscalar_t`` 

56 # rounding). ``tl.div_rn`` is float32-only; for float64 plain ``/`` is 

57 # already correctly rounded. ``b.dtype`` is a compile-time attribute. 

58 if b.dtype == tl.float32: 

59 return tl.div_rn(a, b) 

60 else: 

61 return a / b 

62 

63 

64@triton.jit 

65def _digamma_one(x): 

66 # Vectorized Cephes-style digamma, ported from ATen::native::digamma_one. 

67 PI: tl.constexpr = 3.1415926535897932384626433832795028841971 

68 PSI_10: tl.constexpr = 2.25175258906672110764 

69 

70 is_int = x == tl.floor(x) 

71 neg = x < 0.0 

72 

73 # Reflection x -> 1 - x for negative x. 

74 additional_summand = tl.where( 

75 neg, _div_rn(-PI, tl.sin(PI * x) / tl.cos(PI * x)), tl.zeros_like(x) 

76 ) 

77 y = tl.where(neg, 1.0 - x, x) 

78 

79 # Push y to be >= 10 (C++ ``while (y < 10)``; at most 10 increments since 

80 # y > 1 after the reflection). 

81 result = tl.zeros_like(x) 

82 for _ in range(10): 

83 small = y < 10.0 

84 result = tl.where(small, result - _div_rn(1.0, y), result) 

85 y = tl.where(small, y + 1.0, y) 

86 

87 # Asymptotic series. 

88 a0 = 8.33333333333333333333e-2 

89 a1 = -2.10927960927960927961e-2 

90 a2 = 7.57575757575757575758e-3 

91 a3 = -4.16666666666666666667e-3 

92 a4 = 3.96825396825396825397e-3 

93 a5 = -8.33333333333333333333e-3 

94 a6 = 8.33333333333333333333e-2 

95 z = _div_rn(1.0, y * y) 

96 poly = (((((a6 * z + a5) * z + a4) * z + a3) * z + a2) * z + a1) * z + a0 

97 series = tl.where(y < 1.0e17, z * poly, tl.zeros_like(x)) 

98 

99 out = result + tl.log(y) - _div_rn(0.5, y) - series + additional_summand 

100 # Exact value at the loop boundary. 

101 out = tl.where(y == 10.0, result + PSI_10 + additional_summand, out) 

102 # x == 0 or a negative integer maps to +inf. 

103 out = tl.where((x <= 0.0) & is_int, float("inf"), out) 

104 return out

107@triton.jit 

108def _beta_grad_alpha_small(x, alpha, beta): 

109 # Taylor expansion of the reparameterized Beta(alpha,beta) gradient at x=0. 

110 factor = _digamma_one(alpha) - _digamma_one(alpha + beta) - tl.log(x) 

111 numer = tl.zeros_like(x) + 1.0 

112 inv_alpha = _div_rn(1.0, alpha) 

113 series = _div_rn(numer, alpha) * (factor + inv_alpha) 

114 for i in range(1, 11): 

115 casted_i = i 

116 numer = numer * (casted_i - beta) * x / casted_i 

117 denom = alpha + casted_i 

118 inv_denom = _div_rn(1.0, denom) 

119 series = series + _div_rn(numer, denom) * (factor + inv_denom) 

120 result = x * tl.exp(-beta * tl.log(1.0 - x)) * series 

121 return tl.where(result != result, tl.zeros_like(result), result) 

122

124@triton.jit 

125def _beta_grad_beta_small(x, alpha, beta): 

126 # Taylor expansion of the reparameterized Beta(alpha,beta) gradient at x=1. 

127 factor = _digamma_one(alpha + beta) - _digamma_one(beta) 

128 numer = tl.zeros_like(x) + 1.0 

129 betas = tl.zeros_like(x) + 1.0 

130 dbetas = tl.zeros_like(x) 

131 series = _div_rn(factor, alpha) 

132 for i in range(1, 9): 

133 casted_i = i 

134 numer = numer * (-x / casted_i) 

135 dbetas = dbetas * (beta - casted_i) + betas 

136 betas = betas * (beta - casted_i) 

137 series = series + _div_rn(numer, alpha + casted_i) * (dbetas + factor * betas) 

138 result = -tl.exp((1.0 - beta) * tl.log(1.0 - x)) * series 

139 return tl.where(result != result, tl.zeros_like(result), result)

142@triton.jit 

143def _log1p(v): 

144 # Accurate log(1 + v) without an extern call. 

145 # 

146 # ``tl.log(1.0 + v)`` loses relative accuracy for small ``|v|`` because 

147 # ``1.0 + v`` rounds away the low bits of ``v`` (log(r) ~ v, so the error 

148 # of the rounded sum is amplified by 1/v). The saddle-point branch below 

149 # feeds it ratios that are close to 1 and multiplies the (small) log by a 

150 # large ``alpha``/``beta``, so this matters. For small ``|v|`` use the 

151 # Taylor series; otherwise ``1 + v`` is far enough from 1 that the plain 

152 # log keeps full relative accuracy. 

153 small = tl.abs(v) < 0.25 

154 # Taylor series, truncated after v^10 (error < 1e-8 at |v| = 0.25). 

155 poly = tl.zeros_like(v) 

156 term = v 

157 for k in range(1, 11): 

158 poly = poly + term * (1.0 / k) 

159 term = -term * v 

160 return tl.where(small, poly, tl.log(1.0 + v))

163@triton.jit 

164def _beta_grad_alpha_mid(x, alpha, beta): 

165 # Rice saddle-point expansion for alpha, beta both large. 

166 total = alpha + beta 

167 mean = alpha / total 

168 std = tl.sqrt(alpha * beta / (total + 1.0)) / total 

169 near_mean = (mean - 0.1 * std <= x) & (x <= mean + 0.1 * std) 

170 

171 # Polynomial form valid close to the mode. 

172 b2 = beta * beta 

173 b3 = b2 * beta 

174 b4 = b2 * b2 

175 poly = 47.0 * x * b4 + alpha * ( 

176 (43.0 + 20.0 * (16.0 + 27.0 * beta) * x) * b3 

177 + alpha 

178 * ( 

179 3.0 * (59.0 + 180.0 * beta - 90.0 * x) * b2 

180 + alpha 

181 * ( 

182 (453.0 + 1620.0 * beta * (1.0 - x) - 455.0 * x) * beta 

183 + alpha * (8.0 * (1.0 - x) * (135.0 * beta - 11.0)) 

184 ) 

185 ) 

186 ) 

187 prefactor_num = _div_rn((1.0 + 12.0 * alpha) * (1.0 + 12.0 * beta), total * total) 

188 prefactor_den = 12960.0 * alpha * alpha * alpha * beta * beta * (1.0 + 12.0 * total) 

189 near_result = _div_rn(prefactor_num, (1.0 - x)) * _div_rn(poly, prefactor_den) 

190 

191 # Saddle-point form. 

192 prefactor = _div_rn(-x, tl.sqrt(2.0 * alpha * beta / total)) 

193 stirling = ( 

194 (1.0 + 1.0 / (12.0 * alpha) + 1.0 / (288.0 * alpha * alpha)) 

195 * (1.0 + 1.0 / (12.0 * beta) + 1.0 / (288.0 * beta * beta)) 

196 / (1.0 + 1.0 / (12.0 * total) + 1.0 / (288.0 * total * total)) 

197 ) 

198 term1_num = ( 

199 2.0 * alpha * alpha * (x - 1.0) + alpha * beta * (x - 1.0) - x * (beta * beta) 

200 ) 

201 # ``axbx == alpha*(x-1) + beta*x``, i.e. ``total*x - alpha``. Evaluate it 

202 # through an fma so the rounding of ``total*x`` does not survive: in the 

203 # saddle-point regime ``total*x`` and ``alpha`` nearly cancel, and ``axbx`` 

204 # divides ``term1``/``term3`` and squares into ``term1_den``. 

205 axbx = tl.fma(total, x, -alpha) 

206 term1_den = tl.sqrt(2.0 * alpha / beta) * (total * tl.sqrt(total)) * axbx * axbx 

207 term1 = _div_rn(term1_num, term1_den) 

208 # ``log(alpha / (total*x))`` and ``log(beta / (total*(1-x)))`` are both 

209 # ratios of nearly equal quantities here; rewrite them as log1p of the 

210 # (small, accurately computed) relative difference ``d = total*x - alpha`` 

211 # so the large alpha/beta multipliers below do not amplify the rounding of 

212 # a catastrophic cancellation. 

213 d = axbx 

214 log_a_over_total_x = _log1p(_div_rn(-d, total * x)) 

215 term2 = 0.5 * log_a_over_total_x 

216 term3_num = tl.sqrt(8.0 * alpha * beta / total) 

217 term3 = _div_rn(term3_num, axbx) 

218 log_b_over_total_1mx = _log1p(_div_rn(d, total * (1.0 - x))) 

219 term4_base = beta * log_b_over_total_1mx + alpha * log_a_over_total_x 

220 term4 = _div_rn(1.0, term4_base * tl.sqrt(term4_base)) 

221 term1234 = tl.where( 

222 x < mean, term1 + term2 * (term3 + term4), term1 + term2 * (term3 - term4) 

223 ) 

224 far_result = stirling * prefactor * term1234 

225 

226 return tl.where(near_mean, near_result, far_result)

229@triton.jit 

230def _dirichlet_grad_tile(x, alpha, total): 

231 # Ported from ATen::native::dirichlet_grad_one (Distributions.h); the 

232 # scalar ``if -> return`` cascade becomes end-of-function ``tl.where`` 

233 # selection so no ``tt.map_elementwise`` is needed. 

234 beta = total - alpha 

235 boundary = total * x * (1.0 - x) 

236 

237 small_branch = (x <= 0.5) & (boundary < 2.5) 

238 beta_small_branch = (x >= 0.5) & (boundary < 0.75) 

239 mid_branch = (alpha > 6.0) & (beta > 6.0) 

240 

241 r_small = _beta_grad_alpha_small(x, alpha, beta) 

242 r_beta_small = -_beta_grad_beta_small(1.0 - x, beta, alpha) 

243 r_mid = _beta_grad_alpha_mid(x, alpha, beta) 

244 

245 # Rational-correction branch (final fallback in dirichlet_grad_one). 

246 u = tl.log(x) 

247 a = tl.log(alpha) - u 

248 b = tl.log(total) - a

360 q = q + ua * (C1_200 + b * (C1_201 + b * (C1_202 + b * C1_203)))

383@triton.jit 

384def _dirichlet_grad_func(x, alpha, total): 

385 return _dirichlet_grad_tile(x, alpha, total).to(x.dtype)

388def _dirichlet_grad(x, alpha, total): 

389 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN DIRICHLET_GRAD") 

390 # The ATen reference only implements the AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES path. 

391 assert x.dtype in ( 

392 torch.float32, 

393 torch.float64, 

394 ), f"_dirichlet_grad only supports float32/float64, got {x.dtype}" 

395 return _dirichlet_grad_func(x, alpha, total)

402 torch.float64, 

403 ), f"_dirichlet_grad only supports float32/float64, got {x.dtype}" 

404 _dirichlet_grad_func(x, alpha, total, out0=out) 

405 return out
